meta.scope: Visual language for industrial / tech mods in the vein of Mekanism: clean brushed-steel casings, tiered color accents, readable machine faces, restrained animation, strong functional color coding.

upstream.note: The MIT LICENSE has no exception for assets. The README credits several artists but states no separate terms.

rules.rule: Mekanism textures/models may be copied and modified, but every build and the repo must ship the MIT license text with the upstream copyright line.
rules.check: exists(src/main/resources/licenses/mekanism/LICENSE.txt) and exists(THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md) when provenance has mekanism entries

rules.rule: Every imported or derived file has an entry in art/provenance.yaml (source path, upstream commit, modified yes/no).
Imported assets live in your own namespace (assets/<modid>/), never under assets/mekanism/ (no accidental resource overrides).
rules.check: no files under assets/mekanism/ in your mod

rules.rule: Don't use the Mekanism name or logo in a way that suggests your mod is official or endorsed.
If your mod can run next to Mekanism, change at least the function zone or tint of reused machine faces so players can tell the blocks apart.
Assets from any other source need their own license check and provenance entry; MIT coverage applies to Mekanism's repo only.

principles.name: Readability first
principles.rule: A player must identify block type, tier and state (idle/active/error) from 5 blocks away.

principles.name: Vanilla-compatible pixel art
principles.rule: 16x16 base resolution, hard pixel edges, no photo textures, no gradients without dithering steps.

principles.name: Function drives form
principles.rule: Every visible feature (port, tank, fan, display) implies a function. No greebles without purpose.

principles.name: Consistency over novelty
principles.rule: Shared casing, shared palette ramps, shared port language across all machines in the mod.

principles.name: Calm when idle, alive when working
principles.rule: Idle machines are static; activity is shown by animation, emissive light and sound together.

principles.name: Performance is part of the style
principles.rule: Prefer baked models + animated textures over BlockEntityRenderers. Animation must never cost TPS.

mekanism_reference.description: Measured from Mekanism machine faces (base/, crusher/, enrichment_chamber/, factory/*), 1.21.x @ 4255aa7.

steel_ramp.description: Neutral (pure gray) machine ramp aligned with Mekanism casings, darkest to lightest.

rules.rule: Machine casings are neutral; at least 85% of opaque pixels have HSV saturation <= 0.08 (active/on states >= 70%, SHOULD). Color lives in accents, ports, indicators.
Own-drawn casings may be checked against the exact palette (steel_ramp + tiers + semantic + status + brass).
Neighbouring shades differ by one ramp step; skip at most one step at a hard edge.

tiers.note: Use as hue anchors; build own 4-step ramps around them.

rules.rule: Tier is shown by an accent (trim, stripe, corner pieces, LED band), never by recoloring the whole casing.
rules.check: accent_pixels / opaque_pixels <= 0.25 for tiered block textures

rules.rule: Tier accent placement is identical across all tiers of the same block, only the hue changes.
Generate tier variants from one grayscale accent mask + tint (datagen, tint index or palette swap script).

fluid.meaning: fluid port/tank (actual fluid uses its own tint)

chemical.meaning: chemical port; contents tinted by chemical color

data.meaning: data cable body (hstg_research, white/neutral). gui = data signature color: side-config Data tab tint, GUI data bar, data icon accents. Ports themselves use the port-type colors (Output = Mekanism DARK_BLUE), like items/energy

rules.rule: A semantic color is never reused for decoration. Green always means energy, red/blue always mean input/output.
rules.check: semantic colors only inside regions tagged port|gauge|led|indicator

rules.rule: Never rely on color alone; pair with shape (arrow, notch, icon) for colorblind players.

global_rules.rule: No pure black (#000000) or pure white (#FFFFFF) in opaque casing pixels. Exception — tint bases/overlays (overlay/, *_tint*, *mask*), where white is the tint carrier.
Max 96 distinct opaque colors per 16x16 frame (Mekanism median 59, max 83). Own pixel art aims for <= 32.
Hue-shift ramps (shadows toward blue/violet, highlights toward warm/neutral) instead of pure value changes on colored materials.
Emissive colors are saturated but not neon-on-neon; an emissive pixel must sit next to a steel_0..steel_2 pixel for contrast.

rules.rule: Block faces and items are 16 wide (32 for detailed animated faces); model sheets are power-of-two up to 256. Height is a multiple of width.
rules.check: width in allowed_sizes[folder] and height % width == 0

rules.rule: Alpha is binary (0 or 255) on cutout textures; partial alpha only on textures used with a translucent render type.
Custom-model texture sheets keep texel density at 16 px per block (1 px == 1 u). No mixed densities on one model.
No anti-aliasing, blur, noise filters or upscaled art. Hand-placed pixels only.
rules.check: no isolated pixels with alpha 1..254 on opaque textures

rules.rule: Shade within a face only (bevels, panels). Do not bake directional face shading — the engine already darkens sides and bottom.
Raised elements get a 1 px highlight top/left and a 1 px shadow bottom/right; recessed elements invert this.

casing_anatomy.description: Standard machine casing face (16x16) from outside in.

layers.name: outer_frame
layers.note: 1 px frame; lit top/left, dark bottom/right

layers.name: function_zone
layers.note: front face only: screen, intake, output, port

rules.rule: All machines share the same outer frame and corner treatment so blocks tile as one family.
Brushed-metal texture is max 1 ramp step of variation and runs horizontally on sides, uniformly on top.
Panel seams line up across adjacent faces of the same block (edges meet at the same pixel row).
Exactly one face (front) carries the machine's identifying graphic. Other faces stay family-generic.
Front graphic is readable as a silhouette at 50% scale (think icon, not illustration).
The "on" texture differs only inside the function_zone and indicator pixels; frame and casing are identical.
Implement on-state as an overlay layer (separate texture, emissive) rather than a full duplicate texture.
Side-config/port overlays are separate neutral textures (gray
Port graphic is a 6x6 to 8x8 centered square/ring with a shape cue (inward arrow = in, outward = out, bolt = energy).
Overlays use emissive at reduced brightness (block_light 8–12), never full 15, so they do not glow like lamps.
Mekanism multiblock textures carry ConnectedTexturesMod data (`ctm` key in .mcmeta). Reuse them only if your mod depends on CTM, otherwise strip the key and ship the plain texture.
rules.check: if mcmeta has 'ctm' then dependency CTM declared

material_items.description: Ore-processing chain items share one silhouette language per stage.

rules.rule: Each stage is one grayscale template; per-material variants are tint or palette-swap, not redrawn.
Stages are distinguishable by silhouette alone (grayscale test).
Item sprites keep a 1 px transparent margin and a dark (steel_0 or hue-dark) outline on the lower/right edge.
snake_case, lowercase ASCII, no spaces. Faces from {front, back, side, left, right, top, bottom}, states from {off, on, active, error}. Pick one layout (flat or per-machine folder) for the whole mod.

formats.preferred: vanilla JSON block/item models (datagen-generated where possible)
formats.dynamic_parts: BlockEntityRenderer or baked sub-models for moving parts only

classes.geometry: cube base + 2–6 detail elements (tanks, pipes, hatches)
custom model, clear moving part (rotor, piston)

rules.rule: All element coordinates on the 1 u grid (integers 0–16). Half units only for thin trims, never smaller.
Machine footprint is the full block (0–16 on X/Z) unless the block is explicitly a non-full shape; bottom at y=0.
Element budget — simple ≤ 1, process ≤ 24, generator ≤ 48, transport core+arm ≤ 8 per state.
Element rotations limited to the vanilla set (-45, -22.5, 0, 22.5, 45) on one axis per element.
Faces flush with the block boundary declare `cullface`; hidden internal faces are deleted.
rules.check: faces on boundary have cullface; no face fully occluded by another element

rules.rule: VoxelShape (collision/selection) follows the visual model at 1 u precision; simplified to ≤ 8 boxes.
UVs map 1 px = 1 u, no stretched UVs, no mirrored UVs on text or arrows.
Rotatable machines use blockstate `y` rotation of one north-facing model, not separate models per facing.
Set `render_type` explicitly (solid | cutout | translucent). Glass/tanks use translucent on their own element only.
Emissive elements use NeoForge per-element light data (`neoforge_data.block_light/sky_light`) and `shade: false`.
Item display transforms (gui, ground, fixed, thirdperson, firstperson) are set so the front face is visible in the inventory icon.
Ambient occlusion stays on for casings, off for emissive and thin trims.
Transport blocks use multipart blockstates (core + per-direction arm), arms share one model rotated.
Detail protrudes at most 2 u beyond the casing; anything larger becomes a multiblock or separate block.
Keep the top edge mostly flat so machines stack and line up in rows.
Only use a BlockEntityRenderer if geometry must move; anything 2D is an animated texture.
Animate only while the machine is active; idle state renders the static baked model.
Motion is driven by (gameTime + partialTick), never by wall clock or per-frame increments.
rules.check: no System.currentTimeMillis / frame counters in renderers

rules.rule: Spin-up and spin-down use easing over 20–40 ticks; no instant start/stop of rotating parts.
Speed scales with work rate (upgrades, power input), capped at a speed that still reads as rotation (no strobe/wagon-wheel).

fluid_level.note: interpolate between synced levels, never jump

rules.rule: BER culls beyond 64 blocks (getViewDistance) and draws nothing for invisible/empty parts.
Moving parts are pre-baked models rendered with a pose transform; no per-frame quad building.
Client-only state; server syncs only `active` and work rate, never animation angles.
Override render bounding box for oversized animated parts so they don't pop out at screen edges.
Every animated machine has a matching looped sound and emissive on-state; all three start/stop together.
Particles (steam, sparks) sparingly — max 1 spawn every 10 ticks per machine, client setting to disable.

mekanism_reference.pingpong: common — e.g. 12-frame strip played via an 18-entry frames list (0..11..1)

led_blink.note: 1 s on, 1 s off; error = 10 ticks

conveyor.note: 1 px shift per frame, tile seamlessly

rules.rule: Vertical strip, frame width = texture width, height = width × frame_count.
Loops are seamless: last frame → first frame is a valid next step.
No full-face flashing faster than 3 Hz (frametime×frames for one cycle ≥ 7 ticks) for large bright areas.
rules.rationale: Photosensitivity and visual noise in large machine rooms.

rules.rule: Animate only the function zone; frame and casing pixels are identical in every frame.
Max 32 frames for block textures, 16 for overlays/LEDs (atlas size and memory).
Use `interpolate: true` only for glow/pulse; never for pixel-art motion (it produces blurred mixed colors).
Offset identical animations visually with hold frames per variant to avoid perfectly synchronized walls of blinking blocks, or accept sync deliberately for "network" effects.
For back-and-forth motion use a ping-pong `frames` list instead of duplicating frames in the strip.
Emissive animated layers are separate textures so the base casing stays shaded normally.

base.player_inventory: vanilla layout, y=84 (MekanismContainer.BASE_Y_OFFSET), label at height-94
base.background: mekanism:gui/base.png 256x256, 4 px nine-slice; edges/centre TILED 1:1, never stretched (GuiUtils.blitNineSlicedSized)

side_tabs.button: button.png 200x60 (rows: disabled/normal/hover), 18 px inner at border 4
side_tabs.left: side config (-26,6), transporter (-26,34), energy info (-26,137, 26x26 tabs/energy_info_<unit>.png)

energy_bar.fill: bar/vertical_power.png 4x52 in bar/base.png 5x5 frame (2 px slices)

progress.style: ProgressType (bar 25x9 at (86,38) for electric machines, right 32x8, ...)

slots.layout: electric machine: input (64,17), energy (64,53) + up_arrow (68,38), output (116,35)

upgrade_window.parts: installed list (6,18) 108x50 on element_holder.png with upgrade_selection.png rows (12 px, tinted by upgrade color), info inner_screen (114,18) 59x50 at 0.6 text scale, digital Uninstall (115,54) 56x12, Supported strip (6,68), install slot (175,18) + installing.png (176,37), removed slot (175,72)
upgrade_window.rule: install takes 20 ticks; effects M^(n/8) with M = 10 (speed: ticks x M^-s, energy/t x M^(2s-e); energy: capacity x M^e)

side_config.window: 156x135 at ((w-156)/2, 15), shadow.png 75% alpha 3 px out, close button (6,6)
side_config.faces: 22x22 color buttons, BasicColorButton tint (S-0.1, V+0.1), neighbour block item inside

rules.rule: Slot outline colors in side-config view use exactly the semantic port colors.
Every gauge/bar has a tooltip with exact value and unit (FE, mB, ticks).
Tabs and gauges are shared components reused across all machine screens.
GUI scales cleanly at all vanilla GUI scales; no sub-pixel offsets, no text overlapping widgets at scale 4 with long translations (DE strings are ~30% longer).
Every element and group has a meaningful snake_case name; no "cube", "cube2", "group".
Group by function (casing, function_zone, ports, emissive, moving_<part>).
The Java Block/Item format has no runtime keyframe animation. Each part a BER moves (rotor, piston, drill) is exported as its own model file, e.g. `block/<machine>_rotor.json`.
rules.check: for each BER-animated part: models/block/<machine>_<part>.json exists

rules.rule: Moving-part models are built around their real pivot. Note the pivot (in u) in the outliner name or a sidecar so the renderer rotates around the same point.
The static base model must not contain the moving part (no double-render when active).
Blockbench animations may be used only to preview motion; they are not exported for Java block models.
Paint with the steel ramp + tier/semantic colors loaded as the Blockbench palette, or start from an imported Mekanism face; casings stay neutral (COL-01).
After saving an animated texture, confirm the `.png.mcmeta` exists and matches the preset you meant to use.
Overlays (ports, LEDs, tier masks) are separate textures, not layers merged into the casing.
Texture references in exported JSON use `<modid>:block/<name>`, never absolute paths or `#missing`.
rules.check: all textures values match ^[a-z0-9_]+:(block|item)/[a-z0-9_/]+$ or start with #

rules.rule: The .bbmodel source is saved next to every export so the model can be edited later.

agent_rules.rule: Agents read the current project state before editing and never overwrite an unsaved project without asking.
Agents prefer dedicated MCP tools over script evaluation (e.g. `risky_eval`); script evaluation needs the user's approval.
Agents review a screenshot/preview after each major step (casing, details, textures) when the MCP offers one.

dos.text: Start from Mekanism's base/ casing (via import_mekanism.py) or one own casing template; derive every machine from it.
Generate tier and material variants via tint masks or scripts, not by hand.
Test every texture in-game in a dark room, in daylight and next to vanilla blocks.
Run the grayscale test: is the block still recognizable without color?
Keep a shared .ase/.aseprite palette file; lint textures against it in CI.
Put emissive details in separate overlay layers/elements.
Reuse arms/cores/ports as shared models; only identity faces differ.
Animate with partialTick interpolation and easing.
Use datagen for blockstates, models and item models to keep naming consistent.
Check a 3x3 wall of the block for tiling seams and visual noise.
Preview with common shader packs/resource packs off and on (Iris/Oculus emissive behavior).

donts.text: Don't recolor the whole machine per tier — accent only.
Don't use pure black/white in casings or saturated casing bodies.
Don't use 32x+ textures on plain cube faces or mix texel densities on one model.
Don't bake face-direction shading into textures.
Don't use a BER for anything a .mcmeta animation can do.
Don't use interpolate on pixel-motion animations.
Don't flash large bright areas faster than ~3 Hz.
Don't reuse semantic colors (energy green, input red, output blue) as decoration.
Don't add bolts, pipes or vents with no gameplay meaning.
Don't use sub-0.5 u geometry or arbitrary rotation angles.
Don't leave hidden internal faces or missing cullfaces.
Don't make emissive overlays full brightness 15 unless it is a light source.
Don't ship Mekanism-derived files without the MIT notice and a provenance entry.
Don't put imported textures under assets/mekanism/.
Don't reuse assets from other mods without checking their own license.
Don't sync animation state from server every tick.

texture: Imported? provenance entry + license shipped (LEGAL-01, LEGAL-02)
blockbench: Outliner named (BB-01), moving parts split out (BB-10, BB-12)
